# Disagreement Log — 1 Clement Chapter 44

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Chapter:** 1 Clement 44
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA

---

## Disagreements

**Verse 44:1 — "strife over the name of the bishop's office" vs. "strife over the title of the episcopate" vs. "rivalry over the office of bishop"**
- EMET: "strife over the name of the bishop's office"
- LOGOS: "strife over the title of the episcopate"
- PNEUMA: "rivalry would break out over the office of bishop"
- Note: Greek *eris epi tou onomatos tēs episkopēs* (strife about the name of the episcopate). EMET preserves "name" (*onoma*) which may be significant — the contest is partly over the honorific title, not just the office. LOGOS's "episcopate" is the most technical term.

**Verse 44:2 — "perfect foreknowledge" vs. "complete foreknowledge"**
- EMET: "perfect foreknowledge"
- LOGOS/PNEUMA/SOPHIA: "complete foreknowledge"
- Note: Greek *teleia prognōsis* (perfect/complete foreknowledge). Both "perfect" and "complete" render *teleia*; "perfect" has theological resonance.

**Verse 44:2 — "fall asleep" — all agree**
- Note: Consensus on *koimēthōsin* (to fall asleep = die). The euphemism is preserved across all agents.

**Verse 44:2 — "give provision" vs. "made provision"**
- EMET: "gave provision"
- LOGOS/PNEUMA/SOPHIA: "made provision"
- Note: Minor difference; "made provision" is more idiomatic.

**Verse 44:3 — "other reputable men" vs. "other eminent men" vs. "other men of good standing"**
- EMET: "other reputable men"
- LOGOS/SOPHIA: "other eminent men"
- PNEUMA: "other men of good standing"
- Note: Greek *ellogimois andrasin* (notable, reputable, eminent men). LOGOS "eminent" captures the social standing; EMET "reputable" captures the character dimension.

**Verse 44:3 — "without self-seeking" vs. "unselfishly" vs. "without personal ambition"**
- EMET/SOPHIA: "without self-seeking"
- LOGOS: "unselfishly"
- PNEUMA: "without personal ambition"
- Note: Greek *aplēstōs* (without greed, without self-seeking). "Self-seeking" captures the acquisitive dimension well.

**Verse 44:4 — "thrust aside" vs. "depose" vs. "dismiss"**
- EMET: "thrust aside"
- LOGOS/SOPHIA: "depose"
- PNEUMA: "dismiss"
- Note: Greek *kathistantas* (those being removed). "Depose" is the most precise ecclesiastical term for forced removal from office.

**Verse 44:4 — "bishop's office" vs. "episcopate"**
- EMET/SOPHIA: "bishop's office"
- LOGOS: "episcopate"
- PNEUMA: "bishop's office"
- Note: Greek *episkopē*. Both renderings are accurate; "episcopate" is more technical and precise.

**Verse 44:5 — "elders" vs. "presbyters"**
- EMET/PNEUMA/SOPHIA: "elders"
- LOGOS: "presbyters"
- Note: Greek *presbyteroi*. "Presbyters" is the technical form; "elders" is the translation. In context (parallel to "bishops"), the term is important. SOPHIA prefers "elders" as the standard English translation.

**Verse 44:6 — "we see" vs. "we perceive"**
- EMET: "we see"
- LOGOS/SOPHIA: "we perceive"
- PNEUMA: "we can see"
- Note: Greek *horōmen* (we see, we observe). "Perceive" adds a nuance of insight; "see" is more direct.

---

*Total disagreements: 10*
*Note: Chapter 44 is the culmination of the apostolic succession argument. The most significant translation decisions are: (1) v. 1 "name/title of the bishop's office/episcopate" — EMET's preservation of "name" (*onoma*) may be the most precise; (2) v. 3 "consent of the whole church" — all agents agree this phrase is present; (3) v. 4 "offered the gifts" — all agents agree this refers to eucharistic presidency; (4) v. 5 "elders" vs. "presbyters" — the equivalence of the terms in this context is theologically significant.*
